olga_customer: Hi — hitting intermittent invalid JSON in json_mode responses from /v1/generate. Happens under load, parser fails. Example payload (expected single object but we get merged fields):
```json
{"id":"resp_abc","choices":[{"index":0,"content":{"name":"Alice","age":30}}] }{"id":"resp_def","choices":[{"index":0,"content":{"name":"Bob","city":"NYC"}}]
```
olga_customer: That string above is literally what we saw (two objects concatenated with field fragments interleaved on some requests).
emma_support: Sorry you're seeing this — can you paste the request_id from the response headers and the SDK/curl you used? Also which deployment: Hosted or Dedicated?
olga_customer: request_id=rid_8f9c; hosted region=us-west; using json_mode=true and batching=auto from our node SDK. Sample curl: ```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","mode":"json","input":"...","stream":false}'
```
emma_support: thanks. @raj_engineer can you take a look? :eyes:
raj_engineer: looking. quick Qs: are you using prefix_kv_cache or any server-side caching settings? Also approx concurrency and batch_size when it fails.
olga_customer: We have heavy concurrent users — ~200rps to that endpoint, average batch size 8 on your hosted routing. Not setting explicit prefix_kv_cache on our side.
raj_engineer: got it. sharing early hypothesis: sounds like a race where cached KV/prefix entries from one request are being reused across another during batch stitching, producing concatenated/overlapped JSON fragments. I'll try to reproduce with a small harness.
noah_oncall: FYI infra telemetry shows spikes in batch merging around 2025-10-12T16:02:xx UTC for rid_8f9c. infra-bot: "detected high batch merging activity on cluster gw-usw-3; avg_batch=7.9; kv_cache_hits=0.42"
noah_oncall: I reproduced locally by sending two concurrent requests with similar prefixes and json_mode=true. Repro steps:
```bash
# repro script (simplified)
for i in 1 2; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","mode":"json","input":"User: Hi\nAssistant:","stream":false}' &
done
wait
```
# after a few runs I got concatenated objects like the customer reported
```json
{"id":"resp_1","choices":[{"content":{"name":"Alice"}}]}{"id":"resp_2","choices":[{"content":{"name":"Bob","age":25}}]
```
noah_oncall: root cause looks like buffer reuse during batch composition + missing separation when assembling final JSON blobs.
raj_engineer: thanks. immediate mitigation options: 1) force json_mode requests to single-shot (max_batch=1) on routing layer, 2) disable prefix/KV caching for json_mode requests, 3) sanitize final assembly to ensure separators between objects.
emma_support: which is fastest to push as a mitigation? Customer is blocked (their parser crashes).
raj_engineer: fastest: add a routing rule to set max_batch=1 for any request with mode=json. That avoids interleaving immediately. Disabling prefix cache is also quick but more impactful on latency/cost. We'll push an emergency routing tweak to Hosted and notify customers.
olga_customer: please do the routing tweak — we need a fix ASAP. Also happy to accept a flag on our account to apply it only to our traffic.
raj_engineer: can do per-customer rule. I'll file internal ticket ENG-RUNTIME-4721 and mark P2-High. Noah can you coordinate the hotfix deploy?
noah_oncall: deploying routing override to gw-usw clusters now, targeting next 5 minutes. Will monitor.
infra-bot: "override applied: max_batch=1 for traffic with account_id=acct_782; rollout=gw-usw-3,gw-usw-4; status=deploying"
noah_oncall: monitoring — so far no merged-json reports in the last 10 minutes.
emma_support: updated customer: we've applied a per-account routing override that forces single-batch for json_mode on your account while eng investigates. This will increase per-token latency slightly but prevents corrupted JSON.
olga_customer: thanks — parser is stable now, error rate dropped to 0. We'll keep you posted if anything recurs.
raj_engineer: follow-ups: 1) investigate buffer reuse and add safety checks in batch assembler; 2) consider tagging cache entries with request/session ids to avoid cross-request bleed; 3) add test in our CI that fuzzes concurrent json_mode requests; 4) decide if default behavior should be to not batch json_mode responses. I'll take ownership for a patch and ETA 3 days for a code change to assemble separators; 7 days for full fix with cache tags.
emma_support: thanks team — I'll keep ticket updated and send customer email summarizing mitigation and timeline. :white_check_mark:
olga_customer: appreciate the quick turnaround.
raj_engineer: noted — ENG-RUNTIME-4721 created and assigned to me. Adding unit tests and a small integration harness to reproduce at scale.
noah_oncall: closing loop: if anyone sees new occurrences after the hotfix, ping #eng-runtime immediately.
emma_support: closing thread for now; will reopen if needed. :lock:
